title: add downgrade guard, version pinning and backup/restore hooks to private-installer (rollback tooling)
author: Aisha Raman
release_notes: Adds automatic upgrade safety checks: version pinning, pre-upgrade backup hooks, post-upgrade schema migration checks, and a downgrade guard that prevents incompatible rollbacks. Includes Helm chart and Terraform module updates and documentation for operator rollback procedures.
description:
Context: Customers running Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) have reported two recent upgrade incidents where automatic rollbacks caused data divergence between control-plane metadata and the Postgres schema. This PR adds a set of coordinated safeguards to reduce the risk of unsafe downgrades and to make upgrade/rollback tooling deterministic.

What this change does: Adds (1) version pinning for control-plane components and optional chart overrides, (2) pre-upgrade backup hooks that snapshot Postgres and object storage metadata, (3) a downgrade guard in the installer that checks schema/feature compatibility before allowing a downgrade, and (4) small schema migration verification hooks that run post-migration and can auto-trigger a rollback if validation fails. The change touches Helm charts, Terraform modules, installer CLI, and operator runbooks.

Why: We want safe, auditable upgrades for regulated customers and reliable rollback behavior when a migration fails. This reduces incident blast radius and makes the Private Installer suitable for stricter SLAs.

Implementation notes: The downgrade guard is implemented as an installer preflight step that compares deployed component image tags, schema version in Postgres, and an indexed manifest stored in S3-compatible object storage. Version pinning is configurable via values.yaml (helm) and tfvars (terraform). Backup/restore hooks are implemented as Kubernetes Job templates invoked by the installer; they use the existing backup tool (bin/pg-snapshot) and a new small wrapper that also archives service discovery state. Migration verification runs a set of lightweight SQL invariants and a small python validator (scripts/schema_check.py).

Rollout plan: Feature-flagged by default off. We will enable for early-adopter customers after an opt-in pilot. Detailed upgrade playbook added to docs/upgrade/rollback.md.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on the compatibility matrix in charts/values.schema.yaml and the logic in installer/preflight.py; both contain the critical safety checks. The schema_check script intentionally runs in a read-only mode by default and has a --fix flag reserved for manual operator recovery steps.

Author (Aisha): Switched backup job to use installer-readonly role and updated Terraform to provision the role and credentials via KMS. Added unit test to ensure no write statements are present.
